instruction: Use the terminal to switch the desktop clock to 12-hour format on this Ubuntu system.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

llm_judge_reasons: Getter (get_vm_command_line) runs 'gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface clock-format', which directly reads the GNOME system clock-format setting — exactly the right state to verify the instruction.

Metric (check_include_exclude) receives the rules dict {'include': ['12h'], 'exclude': ['24h']} correctly via get_rule, and checks substring inclusion/exclusion on the gsettings output string — logically correct.
Parameter handling is correct: check_include_exclude accesses rules.get('include', []) and rules.get('exclude', []) directly, matching the dict returned by get_rule with no type-key wrapping bug.
Negative control is strong: initial state is '24h' (confirmed from 19:33 clock in screenshots), so the pre-action state scores 0.0 without any cheating.
No postconfig needed since gsettings reads a persistent system setting, not ephemeral UI state.
Evaluator fully covers the single requirement: clock format switched to 12h.
